variants.prompt: Can the hosts reach the internet?

default.label: Connected
default.summary: The hosts can reach the internet.

variants.defaultRationale: The installation overview calls the Assisted Installer the easiest method when the network is connected, so the shortest path starts there.

alternatives.label: Disconnected or restricted
alternatives.summary: The hosts cannot reach the internet directly.

variants.prompt: Which install method will you use?

default.label: Assisted Installer
default.summary: A web installer with pre-flight checks. On bare metal you still supply the machines, network, load balancer, and storage.

variants.defaultRationale: The overview calls the Assisted Installer the easiest way to install when the network is connected.

alternatives.label: Agent-based installer
alternatives.summary: Download the installer and configure it on the command line.

alternatives.label: Installer-provisioned infrastructure
alternatives.summary: The installer uses each host BMC. You still supply the machines, network, load balancer, and storage.

alternatives.label: User-provisioned infrastructure
alternatives.summary: You prepare the machines, load balancer, DNS, and storage, then generate the install assets.

variants.prompt: Which install method will you use on a disconnected network?

default.label: Agent-based installer
default.summary: The local agent-based installer is the method the overview recommends when the network is disconnected.

variants.defaultRationale: The overview says the Agent-based installer is for disconnected environments, and it says to prefer Assisted Installer only when you do not need that download.

alternatives.label: Installer-provisioned infrastructure
alternatives.summary: The installer can provision from the BMC in a disconnected environment. You still supply the machines and the network.

alternatives.label: User-provisioned infrastructure
alternatives.summary: You prepare the infrastructure yourself. This method supports a disconnected install.

variants.prompt: Must ingress router performance exceed the baseline?

default.label: Baseline performance is enough
default.summary: Keep the default IngressController. No extra load balancer.

variants.defaultRationale: The overview requires an external load balancer only when router performance must exceed the baseline.

alternatives.label: Performance must exceed the baseline
alternatives.summary: Configure an external load balancer so ingress VIP traffic is balanced across IngressController replicas.

citations.locator: 2.1.3. Do you want to use existing components in your cluster?

variants.prompt: Install the cluster in FIPS mode?
variants.defaultRationale: FIPS is optional. The overview says it cannot be turned on after the cluster boots, and the shortest path does not enable it.

alternatives.label: Install in FIPS mode
alternatives.summary: Boot RHCOS in FIPS mode and use a FIPS-capable installation program. This cannot be enabled later.
